query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases? Earlier studies of refractory and transition-metal-based high-entropy alloys primarily examined elemental and compositional effects involving Al, Cr, Si, Ti, and V, but the reported outcomes depended on composition limits, phase readjustment, and processing. This emphasis has not resolved the oxidation behavior of compositionally complex alloys, for which synergistic elemental effects make interpretation difficult. The starting alloy was designed to retain an fcc matrix for formability and has demonstrated notable strength and fatigue performance, so any explanation should account for its integrity without compromising those constraints. Define a controlled comparison that would distinguish the proposed explanation, predict observations relative to the starting-state baseline, identify applicable exposure boundaries and supporting prior evidence, and state an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy (fcc matrix), the governing factor for elevated-temperature degradation in gases is the AM-induced cellular solidification substructure and nanoscale segregation topology, which create percolating Cr-enriched pathways at cell walls and Al/Ti-enriched regions in the cell interiors or interdendritic zones. This topology controls a competition between external chromia-based scale formation and internal oxidation/carburation. In dry oxidizing atmospheres, continuous Cr-rich pathways rapidly nucleate a thin, adherent Cr2O3/spinel scale that limits further attack and preserves the fcc matrix. In humid oxidizing atmospheres, chromia volatilization and disruption (via oxyhydroxide formation) along these pathways expose and accelerate internal oxidation of Al/Ti (forming TiO2 and mixed spinels), increasing oxide scale porosity and spallation. In reducing, carbon-active atmospheres, external oxides are suppressed and the same pathways preferentially admit C (and possibly N), forming TiC/Cr-carbides internally that deplete Al/Ti from strengthening phases and reduce fatigue resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-built laser/PBF additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA with an fcc matrix, high defect density (dislocation cells), hierarchical cellular solidification substructure (submicron cells), elemental microsegregation (Cr enrichment expected at cell walls; Al/Ti enrichment likely in interdendritic/cell interiors), and fine-scale strengthening features consistent with the alloy’s reported notable strength/fatigue performance (e.g., possible L12 Ni3(Al,Ti) precipitates), without bulk phase transformation.
generation.intervention: Controlled elevated-temperature gas exposures that vary oxygen potential and carbon activity to bias the oxidation vs internal attack pathways; plus a microstructural control (homogenization/solutionizing to reduce cellular segregation while retaining fcc matrix) to isolate the role of segregation topology.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 800°C (representative; within 700–950°C boundary). Duration: 24–100 h. Atmospheres: (i) Dry oxidizing: O2 ~0.21 atm, H2O <0.01 atm. (ii) Humid oxidizing: O2 ~0.21 atm, H2O ~0.1 atm. (iii) Reducing/carburizing: H2 ~0.95 atm with CH4 ~0.05 atm (low oxygen potential, positive carbon activity). Flow rates sufficient for gas refresh; specimens polished to similar finish before exposure.
generation.structural_mediator: Interconnected AM cellular wall network enriched in Cr relative to the matrix that provides fast, continuous nucleation pathways for chromia/spinels, coexisting with Al/Ti-enriched regions that preferentially undergo internal oxidation or carbide formation when external chromia is disrupted or suppressed.
generation.mechanism: Dry oxidizing: Cr-enriched cell walls rapidly form a thin, continuous Cr2O3/Ni(Co)Cr2O4 spinel scale that is adherent and reduces cation/anion transport, limiting mass gain and preserving the fcc matrix near-surface. Humid oxidizing: H2O increases chromia volatility (oxyhydroxide formation) and disrupts scale continuity along the same pathways, raising oxygen ingress; exposed Al/Ti-rich regions internally oxidize to rutile TiO2 and mixed spinels, creating porous, less adherent scales and deeper internal oxidation zones, promoting spallation and reducing near-surface fatigue integrity. Reducing/carbon-active: Low oxygen potential suppresses external oxide formation; carbon diffuses preferentially along the segregation network, forming TiC and Cr-carbides internally, depleting Al/Ti from strengthening features (e.g., L12) and increasing near-surface hardness while degrading ductility/fatigue.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-built baseline at 800°C: (i) Dry oxidizing: Lower mass gain rate and a thin, continuous chromia/spinel scale; shallow internal oxidation; minimal change in near-surface hardness; fcc matrix retained. (ii) Humid oxidizing: Greater scale porosity and spallation tendency, higher mass change variability, thicker but less protective mixed oxide with internal TiO2; deeper internal oxidation; reduced near-surface fatigue resistance. (iii) Reducing/carbon-active: Minimal external oxide; formation of TiC/Cr-carbides to tens of microns depth relative to dry oxidizing; increased near-surface hardness and reduction in local ductility; evidence of Al/Ti depletion from strengthening features.
generation.baseline: As-built AM alloy in dry oxidizing atmosphere at 800°C forms a largely continuous Cr2O3/spinel surface scale with limited internal oxidation and retains the fcc matrix and near-surface mechanical integrity over tens of hours.
generation.boundary: Temperature range where chromia is stable and protective (approximately 700–950°C). Below ~600°C kinetics are slow and differences may be difficult to resolve; above ~1000°C Ni/Co oxides/spinels dominate and may overwhelm chromia effects. Protective behavior depends on sufficient Cr enrichment at cell walls; if processing eliminates segregation or alters phase balance (e.g., excessive gamma' coarsening or B2 formation), outcomes may differ. In the reducing case, carburization requires positive carbon activity; in dry reducing H2 without carbon-bearing species, carbide formation may be limited and hydrogen effects may dominate instead.
generation.uncertainty: The exact segregation partitioning of Al/Ti vs Cr to AM cell walls/interiors in this specific composition is not independently verified here, nor is the fraction and stability of any L12 precipitates; thus, the magnitude of differences between dry and humid oxidizing, and between as-built and homogenized conditions, is uncertain. The depth and kinetics of internal carbide formation under the chosen reducing/carbon-active atmosphere are also composition- and processing-sensitive. Without direct evidence records, predicted directions are more confident than sizes.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two microstructural states of identical composition: (A) As-built AM (retaining cellular segregation), and (B) Homogenized/solutionized to reduce cellular segregation while preserving fcc matrix and similar grain size (short solution treatment below incipient melting, optional light aging to recover strength). Expose matched specimens to: dry O2, humid O2 (with controlled H2O), and H2+CH4 reducing/carburizing atmospheres at 800°C for 24–100 h. Use thermogravimetric analysis and interrupted exposures for cross-sectional characterization.
measurements: Mass change vs time (TGA) in each atmosphere
Surface scale thickness, continuity, and porosity (SEM cross-sections, image analysis)
Scale and internal reaction products (XRD; Raman; TEM/EDS; STEM-EELS) to identify Cr2O3, spinels, TiO2, TiC/Cr-carbides
Elemental depth profiles (GDOES/SIMS) for Cr, Al, Ti, C, O across near-surface regions
Near-surface microhardness/nanoindentation profiles to detect carbide-induced hardening
EBSD/EDS mapping to correlate reaction pathways with cellular substructure in as-built vs homogenized
Adhesion/spallation assessment (acoustic emission during TGA, post-exposure tape tests, or scratch testing)
Low-cycle fatigue screening of exposed coupons to assess near-surface degradation trends
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if any of the following are observed: (1) In dry O2, the as-built state does not show equal or lower mass gain and more continuous chromia/spinel scales than the homogenized state; (2) In humid O2, the as-built state does not show greater internal oxidation depth and higher spallation tendency than the homogenized state; (3) In H2+CH4, the as-built state does not show deeper TiC/Cr-carbide penetration and larger near-surface hardness increase than the homogenized state; or (4) Scale/reaction products do not align with Cr2O3/spinels in dry O2, mixed oxides with TiO2 in humid O2, and internal carbides in reducing/carbon-active conditions.
